comments.scripts: Every script must run in both POSIX sh and Windows cmd, because fog-node runs on any OS that runs Node. Do not use VAR=value prefixes, ./path executables, or quotes around echo text. start uses --prod, and Sails then sets NODE_ENV itself. lint calls eslint from node_modules/.bin. The test port and the grunt switch are in test/lifecycle.test.js.
comments.custom-tests: The mocha suite lifts a real Sails app (options in test/lifecycle.test.js). Port 1338 keeps it off 1337 so the suite can run while a dev server is up. Turning the grunt hook off skips the asset pipeline: it is irrelevant to these route tests, and letting it run makes sails-linker rewrite the <script>/<link> block in views/layouts/layout.ejs from whatever happens to be in .tmp — on a fresh clone or CI checkout that directory is empty, so `npm test` would silently strip every vendor tag out of a tracked file. --recursive is required or test/route/ is skipped; --exit is required because Sails leaves handles open after lower().
comments.test:ui: Lifts fog-node with grunt ON and drives Chromium through every routed page (tools/smoke/ui.js). It catches a broken UI dependency that npm test cannot see, because npm test never builds or loads the UI. Needs MongoDB, Redis, npm run setup:dev, and `npx playwright install chromium` once.
comments.test:install: Runs the real installer from an answers file, lifts in production mode, signs in, and checks the socket origins (tools/smoke/install.js). CI never ran the installer before; chalk 6 broke it with every check green. Needs MongoDB and Redis. ws (devDependencies) drives the socket handshake.
comments.migrate: Moves the database from the schema revision in its schema Setting up to the revision in schema below, running each migrations/<n>.js in order (tools/migrate/index.js). It asks about a database backup first: that backup is the rollback. docs/install.md 'Update fog-node' runs it after git pull and npm ci.
comments.schema: The latest schema revision, the highest migrations/<n>.js. tools/lib/config.js getMergedSettings merges this file over config/local.js, so the code names its own revision. A new install records it (tools/setup/lib/schema.js) and so never runs a revision on its empty database.
comments.overrides: Force-patch vulnerable transitive deps pinned by the abandoned sails-hook-grunt/grunt-contrib-less build chain. npm audit fix can't reach them because their parents are unmaintained. Keys of the form 'pkg@N' pin one major at a time, so each consumer keeps the major it was written against. 'less' is forced to 4.x: grunt-contrib-less@1.3.0 asks for less ~2.6.0, but less >=4.6 dropped its bundled HTTP importer, which is what dragged in the unpatchable 'request' and 'image-size' advisories — 'grunt less:dev' output was verified byte-identical before and after that bump. babel-traverse@6 is knowingly left vulnerable: it comes from babel-core@6 inside sails-hook-grunt, there is no 6.x patch, and dropping it would mean dropping asset transpilation from the prod build.

scripts.test: npm run lint && npm run custom-tests && echo Done.
scripts.lint: eslint . --max-warnings=0 --report-unused-disable-directives && echo Your .js files look good.
